name: use.computer

modes.label: Reserved M4 Mac mini, priced per macOS VM slot (2 VMs per Mac)

sizes.name: split: macOS VM slot = half of a reserved M4 Mac mini (5 CPU / 8 GiB)
whole: one VM per reserved Mac (10 CPU / 16 GiB)

modes.commit_note: Reservation = N Mac minis x X hours (X >= 24), paid up front. Sandboxes inside a reservation are free to create/destroy; the Macs return to the pool when end_at passes.
modes.note: Homepage: "$0.90/hr per Mac", "reserve for 24 hours or more, up to 2 VMs at a time per Mac". Docs: each Mac mini is a stock M4 16 GB / 512 GB SSD and the 2 VMs get "4 cores + 8 GB each". Encoded per VM slot at $0.45/h (= $0.90/2), which assumes VMs are paired; an odd VM count pays for an idle slot. Per-VM disk share not published. min 24 h per reservation (Apple SLA). Hourly granularity after the 24 h minimum is confirmed (OpenAPI: integer hours, minimum 24); an active reservation can be shortened (end >= 24 h after start and >= 5 min from now) with the remaining-time delta returned as account credit, or grown pro rata. 2026-09-28 (patch v3-computer-use): OpenAPI VMLayout: split (default) = two 5 CPU / 8 GiB VMs, whole = one 10 CPU / 16 GiB VM (legacy whole may keep 12 GiB), same per-Mac price. 24 h minimum applies per Mac reservation, not per VM creation.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go reservations
plans.note: No plan fee. Production fleet "currently has 28 Mac minis live" (docs), i.e. at most ~56 concurrent VMs unless more are added.

features.ip_note: No browser-automation API, stealth, CAPTCHA or proxy options documented; browsers (e.g. Safari) are driven via the macOS desktop/shell API.

caveats: Rate resolved 2026-09-29: the live API config that drives the dashboard price calculator returns hourly_rate_cents 90 ($0.90/h per Mac, matching the homepage); the dashboard computes total = Macs x hours x rate. The docs' $1.91/h (Quick start, Lifecycle, llms-full.txt) is stale text.

Billing boundary is the Mac reservation, not the sandbox: you pay 24 h minimum per Mac even for a 10-minute session. Encoded as min_billed_seconds 86400 per VM slot; reserving continuously for the month (730 h) is cheaper than re-reserving daily only when sessions span >~20 h/day.
VM slot price assumes both VM slots of each Mac are used; 1 VM per Mac costs $0.90/h.
VM shape by layout (OpenAPI VMLayout): split 5 CPU / 8 GiB x2 per Mac (default) or whole 10 CPU / 16 GiB x1; larger workloads cannot run. Docs prose says 4 cores + 8 GB per VM (older text).
cold_start_ms 1000 = vendor claim "<1s warm boot" on pre-booted reserved Macs, not measured.
Snapshot storage, egress and regions not published (null). Support contact is support@daytona.io; Daytona routes macOS sandboxes here.

Licensing: Apple permits Mac leasing for "Permitted Developer Services"; general computer-use agent workloads are a grey zone. Apple macOS SLA: leasing a Mac requires a minimum lease of 24 consecutive hours with sole use by the lessee, and allows at most 2 additional macOS VMs per Mac.

Idle VMs (~2 min without HTTP/SSH/VNC) are reaped and replaced by a fresh clone; the Mac reservation keeps billing. Snapshots are portable disk images, no memory resume. Docs rate $1.91/h per Mac re-confirmed on docs.use.computer/docs/concepts 2026-09-28; homepage $0.90 could not be re-rendered this pass, so the conflict stands (at $1.91 the bill is 2.12x).

Payment is prepaid only: reservations are paid from a credit balance or Stripe checkout; credit packs $1-$1,000. No postpaid/overage; if credits are insufficient the reservation (or edit) is refused (HTTP 402).

Terms (Crucible Fund LLC, effective 2026-06-03): fees are billed up front for the full committed period and are non-refundable, including unused reservations and early termination; promotional credits may be modified or withdrawn at any time.
VM layout 'split' (default, two 5 CPU / 8 GiB VMs) or 'whole' (one 10 CPU / 16 GiB VM) at the same per-Mac price; layout changes need zero active sandboxes.

fleet.raise: Self-serve reservations are capped by currently free Macs (API returns 409 reservation_capacity_unavailable); API-key (SDK) reservations are limited to 1 Mac each; bulk fleets or long-term capacity by email request from the dashboard.
fleet.verification: Signup provides $100 starter credit with no card.
fleet.notes: Reservations are physical Macs for at least 24 hours, each allowing 2 simultaneous sandbox VMs. No account-wide reservation limit verified. Do not confuse provider inventory or per-host two-VM licence limit with account quota; stock and credits constrain fleets.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When you `delete()` (or your sandbox times out), the gateway throws away the dirty VM and clones a fresh one in the background.
snapshot_auto.note: Idle-reaped (ephemeral=true, ~2 min idle) or timed-out sandboxes and all sandboxes at reservation end_at are destroyed, not saved. State survives only via an explicit snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: macOS snapshots are portable disk deltas. When you create one, the gateway pulls the snapshot artifact from the source Mac Mini; when you launch from it, the gateway pushes that artifact to whichever reserved Mini claims the new VM.
snapshot_on_demand.note: POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/snapshots on a running sandbox ('Preserves disk state'); disk only, no memory. New sandboxes boot from it via create(snapshot=version) on any reserved Mac (template/fork, homepage: 'Snapshot a sandbox. Fork it instantly.'). Must match reservation layout and base image.

harness_api.quote: The `agents` extra installs the agent runtime plus model-provider dependencies (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, LiteLLM).
harness_api.note: The prebuilt computer-use agents (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OSWorld/generic via LiteLLM) run client-side in your Python process and drive the VM through the mouse/keyboard/screenshot API; no API to start/stream/resume an agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) inside the VM. Trajectory replay API (POST /v1/me/tasks/{id}/replay) re-executes recorded human actions, not an agent.

ingress_rules.quote: `vnc_url` from create or snapshot restore contains a sandbox-scoped viewer token, not your account key. The link expires within one hour, or earlier at the reservation's `end_at`
ingress_rules.note: No public ports/preview URLs. Access only through the authenticated gateway: SSH via a WebSocket proxy to sshd (API-key auth; supports -L port forwarding), VNC via expiring sandbox-scoped tokens ('Anyone holding the link can view and control that sandbox until it expires'). No IP allowlists or custom port exposure. Note PyPI README still warns vnc_url contains the account key (older SDK text).

secret_proxy.quote: sign into accounts (email, GitHub, a web app)
secret_proxy.note: No secret store or credential-injection proxy. Docs recommend signing into accounts by hand over VNC and baking the logins into a disk snapshot, i.e. credentials live inside the VM.

volume_attach.quote: `disk_gib` must be the image's disk size: disks are not resized at create.
volume_attach.note: Full OpenAPI spec has no volume/mount endpoints; storage is the VM image disk on the Mac's 512 GB SSD; files move via upload/download APIs.

volume_shared.note: No volume/mount endpoints exist in the full OpenAPI spec at all (grep for volume/mount/shared returns nothing); storage is the VM image disk on the Mac's local SSD. Since there is no volume concept at all, there cannot be a shared-volume feature. Matches card's own feature_evidence for volume_attach.

isolation.quote: The macOS warm pool is built on a fork of lume, the VM orchestrator from cua... the Sequoia base image and the initial VZ plumbing came from there.
isolation.note: Apple Virtualization.framework (VZ) macOS VMs on dedicated M4 Mac minis; card already sets this.

image_oci.quote: disk_gib must be the image's disk size: disks are not resized at create.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sandboxes boot from the provider's own macOS VM images/snapshots (VZ disk images), no Docker/OCI image import; card's custom_image:true refers to macOS snapshot images, not OCI.

anti_bot.quote: Infrastructure for agents that use computers. Instant macOS sandboxes on dedicated Apple M4 Mac minis, driven via Python and TypeScript SDKs.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no stealth/fingerprinting features documented; product is a raw macOS computer-use sandbox, not a browser-automation/anti-detect product.

captcha_solving.quote: Infrastructure for agents that use computers. Instant macOS sandboxes on dedicated Apple M4 Mac minis, driven via Python and TypeScript SDKs.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving service documented; browsers are just apps run inside the macOS VM via the desktop/shell API.

fork_running.quote: Captures a macOS sandbox as a snapshot. Preserves disk state. Snapshots... POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxID}/snapshots
fork_running.note: Snapshot creation (the mechanism behind fork) is called on a running sandbox without stopping/pausing it first; disk-only, not memory.

pause_resume.quote: When you delete() (or your sandbox times out), the gateway throws away the dirty VM and clones a fresh one in the background.
pause_resume.note: No pause/resume API; lifecycle is create/delete plus an idle timeout that destroys the sandbox (state kept only via explicit snapshot), not a pause/resume of a live VM.

wake_on_request.quote: The server defaults new sandboxes on a reserved Mac to the reservation lifetime... Set ephemeral: true to opt into the two-minute idle timeout.
wake_on_request.note: Idle sandboxes are destroyed (and a fresh warm VM is cloned for the next caller) rather than put to sleep and auto-woken by an incoming request; there is no sleeping-machine-wakes-on-traffic mechanism.

live_resize.quote: Any other size resizes a warm VM and boots it, which takes as long as a macOS boot (a minute or two); the response says boot: "cold".
live_resize.note: Changing CPU/RAM requires rebooting the VM (cold boot), not a live in-place resize of a running machine.

own_agent_api.quote: Replay boots a fresh sandbox, runs the setup script, and re-executes the recorded actions. A live VNC link lets you watch the run; if the task has a grader, the reward is reported when the replay completes.
own_agent_api.note: The Trajectories feature records human demonstrations and replays the exact recorded actions (no autonomous goal-driven agent); the optional SDK computer-use agents run client-side using third-party model APIs, not a first-party hosted task-agent API.

mcp_server.quote: Both SDKs (Python on PyPI, TypeScript on npm) expose the same macOS sandbox surface — create() for macOS sandboxes, plus mouse, keyboard, screenshot, exec, files, recording, and the UI tree.
mcp_server.note: No MCP server is mentioned anywhere in the docs, SDK READMEs, or OpenAPI spec; only Python/TypeScript SDKs and a raw HTTP API are offered.

lang_python.quote: The Python SDK is published on PyPI. pip install daytona-use-computer
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK for driving sandboxes.

lang_node.quote: TypeScript (@daytona/use-computer) exposes the same surface; see SDK & API.
lang_node.note: First-party TypeScript/Node SDK, published on npm.

public_ipv4.note: Access to a sandbox is only via the gateway's authenticated SSH/VNC WebSocket proxies; no public IPv4 address is assigned to the sandbox itself.

inbound_https.quote: With WebSocket upgrade headers, upgrades and bridges binary frames to the sandbox VM's sshd (port 22)... VNC connection metadata for the sandbox.
inbound_https.note: No feature to expose arbitrary HTTP(S) ports/URLs on the sandbox; only SSH and VNC are proxied through the gateway with short-lived tokens.

egress_http_rules.quote: macOS Computer Use API — create sandboxes, control input, take screenshots, record sessions.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the API surface is sandbox lifecycle + input/screenshot control; no HTTP method/path-level egress rules exist.

guest_firewall.quote: Instant macOS sandboxes on dedicated Apple M4 Mac minis
guest_firewall.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the guest OS is macOS (uses pf, not nftables/iptables); no Linux guest firewall applies, and no firewall control is documented.

open_source.quote: The macOS warm pool is built on a fork of lume, the VM orchestrator from cua... Thanks to the cua team for open-sourcing it.
open_source.note: The core use.computer gateway/product itself is closed-source; it is built on top of the open-source `lume` VM orchestrator (from the cua project), which is not the same as the product being open source.

eu_data_residency.quote: Reservations are physical Macs for at least 24 hours
eu_data_residency.note: No regions/data-residency feature documented anywhere; fleet is a fixed pool of Mac minis (docs: '28 Mac minis live') with no region selection, so EU residency cannot be guaranteed.

max_session_h.quote: The server defaults new sandboxes on a reserved Mac to the reservation lifetime when the create request omits ephemeral: they live until you delete them or the reservation reaches end_at.
max_session_h.note: A non-ephemeral sandbox runs until you delete it or the (extendable) reservation ends; there is no fixed per-session hour cap distinct from the reservation itself.

persistent_disk.quote: When you `delete()` (or your sandbox times out), the gateway throws away the dirty VM and clones a fresh one in the background. The next caller already has a warm VM waiting.
persistent_disk.note: Idle-reaped (~2 min idle) or timed-out sandboxes and all sandboxes at reservation end_at are destroyed; disk does not survive stop/pause automatically. Only an explicit snapshot (disk-only, via POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/snapshots) preserves files, and restoring it creates a new sandbox rather than resuming the old one in place. Default on timeout/idle/end_at is delete; opt in to snapshot to keep files.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: macOS snapshots are portable disk deltas.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots (the only fork/restore mechanism) are disk-only deltas; no memory or running-process state is captured or restored. Confirmed also by the card's own caveat: 'Snapshots are portable disk images, no memory resume.'

docker_inside.note: Full OpenAPI surface (auth, sandboxes, snapshots, display/vnc, ssh, exec, trajectories, credits) has no Docker/container-runtime endpoints, and no docs page (llms-full.txt, concepts, sdk, quickstart) mentions Docker or container support. The product is a macOS desktop-automation VM, not a container host; not offered.

nested_virt.quote: Choose the Mac model when reserving with `mac_model`: `m4` (the default; 10 cores, 16 GiB) or `m4-pro` (12 or more cores, 24 GiB).
nested_virt.note: No mention anywhere in docs/OpenAPI of nested virtualization, /dev/kvm, or running VMs/emulators inside the sandbox. The sandbox is itself a macOS VM on Apple's Virtualization framework on M4/M4 Pro silicon; nested virtualization support is not advertised or documented. Not offered.

agent_harnesses.quote: The `agents` extra installs the agent runtime plus model-provider dependencies (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, LiteLLM).
agent_harnesses.note: Those are client-side computer-use agent loops (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/OSWorld via LiteLLM) that drive the VM's mouse/keyboard/screenshot API from your own Python process; no coding-agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) is preinstalled or offered as a template inside the VM. Not offered.

gpu.quote: A reservation is a contract for N Mac minis for X hours. You pay up front (hourly rate x N x X): $0.90/hr per M4 Mac, $1.97/hr per M4 Pro Mac.
gpu.note: The only offered machines are M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini VM slots; no GPU instance type exists in docs, pricing, or the OpenAPI catalog. Outside the product's scope (macOS desktop-automation VMs, not a GPU compute cloud).

windows.quote: Instant macOS sandboxes for computer-use agents.
windows.note: The product is exclusively macOS VMs on Apple Mac mini hardware (Apple's macOS software license/SLA governs the whole offering); no Windows machine type is offered anywhere in docs, pricing, or the API. Outside the product's scope.

self_host.quote: So use.computer sells reservations: you reserve one or more physical Mac minis for at least 24 hours, and then create/destroy as many sandboxes as you need inside that reservation.
self_host.note: The service is delivered only as a hosted reservation on use.computer's own fleet of physical Mac minis; no self-hosted/on-prem deployment option, downloadable server, or open-source core is mentioned anywhere in docs, OpenAPI, or the homepage. Not offered.

byoc.quote: Activation binds physical Mac mini IPs to your reservation.
byoc.note: Machines are specific physical Apple Mac minis owned/leased by use.computer under Apple's macOS hardware-leasing terms; there is no mechanism to deploy the service into a customer's own cloud account (Apple's SLA in fact requires the lessor to control the hardware). No BYOC option is mentioned anywhere in docs, pricing, or OpenAPI. Not offered.

egress_ip_type.quote: A reservation is a contract for N Mac minis for X hours... Activation binds physical Mac mini IPs to your reservation.
egress_ip_type.note: Each dedicated physical Mac mini's IP is bound exclusively to your reservation for its duration (>=24h, extendable); VM egress goes out through that dedicated host's datacenter IP, fixed for the life of the reservation, not a shared/rotating pool. Derived from the reservation/isolation model, since no separate networking page documents NAT/egress IP behavior explicitly.

egress_allowlist.quote: macOS Computer Use API — create sandboxes, control input, take screenshots, record sessions.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the full OpenAPI surface (auth, sandboxes, snapshots, display/vnc, ssh, exec, trajectories, credits) has no egress/allowlist/security-group endpoints, and no docs page mentions outbound traffic controls. The product is a macOS desktop-automation VM rental, not a network-security product.

static_egress_ip.quote: Activation binds physical Mac mini IPs to your reservation.
static_egress_ip.note: The physical Mac mini (and its IP) is dedicated solely to your reservation for its whole duration; outbound traffic from VMs on that Mac therefore uses a fixed host IP for as long as the reservation lasts (it is not guaranteed to be the same IP across separate reservations).

sso.quote: init() loads /v1/config, boots Supabase auth, wires the router, and renders the first route.
sso.note: Account login is handled via Supabase auth (their own login/settings views); no SAML/OIDC single-sign-on option for customer organizations is mentioned anywhere in docs, OpenAPI, or the SPA router views (login, reservations, reservation, checkout, settings only).

usage_api.quote: GET /v1/me/billing endpoint returns user's credit balance, ledger entries, and active metered usage including per-sandbox usage with charged_cents, but requires UserJWT (browser session), not API keys. The billing boundary is the Mac reservation (24h minimum), not individual sandboxes.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; The /v1/me/billing endpoint shows per-sandbox usage with charged_cents (cost), but it requires browser authentication (UserJWT), not programmatic API key access (uc_live_* keys). The customer SDK/API keys cannot access per-sandbox billing via any endpoint (GET /v1/sandboxes/{id} returns no cost data). Billing is actually at the reservation level, not per-sandbox. A platform billing system cannot programmatically retrieve per-customer or per-sandbox usage via API key or CLI.

locations_quote: Reservations are physical Macs for at least 24 hours, each allowing 2 simultaneous sandbox VMs. No location/region selection documented.
